label: prop:HS
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:HS}
		Suppose $\mathbb{H}=\mathbb{C}$ and that \eqref{eq:HS-condition_U} is not true. Then $\operatorname{hsp}(\mathcal{V},\mathcal{T})$ is violated for a generic subspace $\mathcal{V}\subset\mathbb{H}^n$ of dimension $d$.
head: environment

label: prop:HS-sign
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: theorem:HS-SA
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{theorem:HS-SA}
		Let $(d_1,\dots,d_\ell)$ be a dimension configuration and $\mathscr{I}=(\mathcal{I}_1,\dots,\mathcal{I}_s)$ an ordered set of subsets of $[\ell]$. Let $d:=\max_{j\in[s]} d_{\mathcal{I}_j}$. Suppose $\operatorname{rank}(\tau)\geq 2d$ for every $\tau\in\mathcal{T}$. Then $\operatorname{hsp}(\overline{\mathcal{A}_{\mathscr{I}}},\mathcal{T})$ holds for a generic subspace arrangement $\mathcal{A}=(\mathcal{V}_1,\dots,\mathcal{V}_{\ell})$ with $\dim(\mathcal{V}_i)=d_i$, whenever \eqref{eq:HS-condition_U} holds. Similarly, $\operatorname{hsp}_\pm(\overline{\mathcal{A}_{\mathscr{I}}},\mathcal{T})$ holds for a generic subspace arrangement $(\mathcal{V}_1,\dots,\mathcal{V}_{\ell})$ with $\dim(\mathcal{V}_i)=d_i$, whenever \eqref{eq:HS-condition_U_sign} holds.
head: environment
name: homomorphic sensing of a subspace arrangement

title: Remark
body_md:
Affine subspaces are very important in applications, because data tend to come biased away from the origin; see for example the case of affine real phase retrieval \cite{Gao-AAM2018} or arrangements of affine subspaces in clustering \cite{Tsakiris-TPAMI2018}. 
Given an affine subspace $\mathcal{V}+b$ of $\mathbb{H}^n$ one obtains immediately a result about $\operatorname{hsp}(\mathcal{V}+b,\mathcal{T})$ by applying Theorem \ref{eq:HS-condition_U} to the $(d+1)$-dimensional linear subspace $\mathcal{V}+\operatorname{Span}(b)$. One obtains a homomorphic sensing result for an arrangement of affine subspaces in a similar manner by applying Theorem \ref{theorem:HS-SA} to $(\mathcal{V}_1 + b_1,\dots,\mathcal{V}_\ell+b_\ell)$. 
An approach which takes into explicit consideration the nature of the affine subspaces will be considered in a future manuscript.
head: environment

label: corollary:HS-R^n
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{corollary:HS-R^n}
		For a generic matrix $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\roman*)]
			\item $m\geq 2n\Rightarrow\operatorname{hsp}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathcal{S}_m A)$ \cite{Tsakiris-ICML2019,Unnikrishnan-TIT18,Han-ACHA2018,Dokmanic-SPL2019}. 
			\item  $r\geq 2n\Rightarrow\operatorname{hsp}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathcal{S}_{r,m} A)$  \cite{Tsakiris-ICML2019,Unnikrishnan-TIT18,Han-ACHA2018}.
			\item  $m\geq 2n\Rightarrow \operatorname{hsp}_{\pm}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathcal{B}_m A)$ \cite{Balan-ACHA2006,Dokmanic-SPL2019}.
			\item\label{C1.4} $r\geq 2n\Rightarrow\operatorname{hsp}_{\pm}(\mathbb{R}^n,\mathcal{S}_{r,m}\mathcal{B}_m A)$ \cite{Tsakiris-ICML2019,Lv-ACM2018}.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: unlabeled sensing and real phase retrieval

label: corollary:HS-k-sparse
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{corollary:HS-k-sparse}
		For a generic matrix $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $k\leq n$
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\roman*)]
			\item\label{C2.1} $m\geq 2k\Rightarrow\operatorname{hsp}(\overline{\mathcal{K}_{\mathscr{I}}},\mathcal{S}_m A)$.
			\item\label{C2.2}  $r\geq 2k\Rightarrow\operatorname{hsp}(\overline{\mathcal{K}_{\mathscr{I}}},\mathcal{S}_{r,m} A)$.
			\item\label{C2.3} $m\geq 2k\Rightarrow \operatorname{hsp}_{\pm}(\overline{\mathcal{K}_{\mathscr{I}}},\mathcal{B}_m A)$ \cite{Wang-ACHA2014,Akccakaya-arXiv2013v2}.
			\item\label{C2.4} $r\geq 2k\Rightarrow\operatorname{hsp}_{\pm}(\overline{\mathcal{K}_{\mathscr{I}}},\mathcal{S}_{r,m}\mathcal{B}_m A)$.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment
name: sparse unlabeled sensing and sparse real phase retrieval

label: lem:flag
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:flag}
Let $\phi: \operatorname{F}_{\mathbb{H}}(d_0,d,n) \rightarrow \operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb{H}}(d,n)$ be the canonical projection that sends $(\mathcal{V}_0,\mathcal{V})$ to $\mathcal{V}$. If $\mathscr{U}$ is a non-empty Zariski open subset of $\operatorname{F}_{\mathbb{H}}(d_0,d,n)$, then the image $\phi(\mathscr{U})$ contains a non-empty Zariski open subset of $\operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb{H}}(d,n)$.
head: environment

label: lemma:subspaces_intersect_subspace
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:subspaces_intersect_subspace}
Given algebraic varieties $\mathcal{Q}_1,\dots,\mathcal{Q}_t$ in $\mathbb{C}^n$ of dimensions $r_1,\dots,r_t$, each defined by homogeneous polynomials, there exists a $\mathbb{C}$-subspace $\mathcal{V} \in \operatorname{Gr}_{\mathbb{C}}(d,n)$ with $\dim(\mathcal{Q}_j\cap\mathcal{V})=\max\{r_j+d-n,0\}$ for any $j\in[t]$.
head: environment

label: lemma:homogeneous
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:homogeneous}
Let $0 \subsetneq \mathcal{Z}\subset \mathcal{Y}$ be two algebraic varieties of $\mathbb{C}^n$ defined by homogeneous polynomials. If $\dim(\mathcal{Y}\backslash \mathcal{Z})>n-d$, then a generic subspace $\mathcal{V}\subset \mathbb{C}^n$ of dimension $d$ intersects $\mathcal{Y}\backslash \mathcal{Z}$.
head: environment

label: lemma:lemma5ofHS
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:lemma5ofHS}
Let $n,d$ be positive integers with $n \ge 2d$. Let $\tau: \mathbb{C}^n \rightarrow \mathbb{C}^n$ be a $\mathbb{C}$-linear map with $\dim(\mathscr{E}_{\tau,\lambda})\leq n-d$ for every $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$. Then there is a $\mathbb{C}$-subspace $\mathcal{V}$ of $\mathbb{C}^n$ of dimension $d$ such that $\dim(\mathcal{V}+\tau(\mathcal{V}))=2d$.
head: environment

label: lemma:U_dimensionbound
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:U_dimensionbound}
		Let $\Pi_1,\Pi_2\in\mathcal{S}_m$, $S_1,S_2\in\mathcal{S}_{r,m}$, and $B_1,B_2\in\mathcal{B}_m$ be permutations, rank-$r$ selections,  and sign matrices, respectively.
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\roman*)]
			\item $m\geq 2n\Rightarrow \dim(\mathcal{U}_{\Pi_1,\Pi_2})\leq m-n$.
			\item $r\geq 2n\Rightarrow\dim(\mathcal{U}_{S_1,S_2})\leq m-n$.
			\item $m\geq 2n\Rightarrow \dim(\mathcal{U}_{B_1,B_2}^{\pm})\leq m-n$.
			\item $r\geq 2n\Rightarrow \dim(\mathcal{U}_{S_1B_1,S_2B_2}^{\pm})\leq m-n$.
		\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: prop:E<=n-d
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:E<=n-d}
In addition to the hypotheses of Theorem \ref{theorem:HS}, further assume $\dim (\mathscr{E}_{(\tau_1,\tau_2),1})\leq n-d$. Then there is an $n$-dimensional subspace $\mathcal{V}^*$ of $\mathbb{H}^n$ which satisfies $\dim (\tau_1(\mathcal{V}^*)+\tau_2(\mathcal{V}^*))=2d$.

label: lemma:chain-property
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:chain-property}
		For any non-negative integer $j$ we have i) $\mathcal{R}_{j+1}\subset \mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j
		\subset\mathcal{R}_j$, ii) $\mathcal{F}_{j+1}\subset \mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j\subset \mathcal{F}_j$, 
		iii) $\mathcal{G}_{j+2}\subset\mathcal{G}_{j+1}$ and iv) $\tau_1(\mathcal{R}_{j+1})=\tau_2(\mathcal{F}_{j+1})=\mathcal{G}_{j+1}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
i) and ii) are directly by definition and so is $\mathcal{R}_{j+1}\cap\mathcal{F}_{j+1}\subset \mathcal{R}_{j}\cap\mathcal{F}_{j}$. This latter implies
		\begin{align*}			\mathcal{G}_{j+2}=\tau_1(\mathcal{R}_{j+1}\cap\mathcal{F}_{j+1})\cap\tau_2(\mathcal{R}_{j+1}\cap\mathcal{F}_{j+1})\subset \tau_1(\mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j)\cap \tau_2(\mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j)=\mathcal{G}_{j+1}.
		\end{align*}
We now show that $\tau_1(\mathcal{R}_{j+1})= \mathcal{G}_{j+1}$. From $\mathcal{R}_{j+1}\subset \tau_1^{-1}(\mathcal{G}_{j+1})$ we have $\tau_1(\mathcal{R}_{j+1})\subset \tau_1(\tau_1^{-1}(\mathcal{G}_{j+1})) \subset \mathcal{G}_{j+1}$. For the reverse direction $\mathcal{G}_{j+1}\subset \tau_1(\mathcal{R}_{j+1})$ let $z\in\mathcal{G}_{j+1}= \tau_1(\mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j)\cap \tau_2(\mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j)$. In particular $z\in\tau_1(\mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j)$ so there is some $w\in\mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j$ with $\tau_1(w)=z$. Then $w\in\tau_1^{-1}(z)\cap \mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j$. But $\tau_1^{-1}(z)\subset\tau_1^{-1}(\mathcal{G}_{j+1})$ and so $w\in\tau_1^{-1}(\mathcal{G}_{j+1})\cap \mathcal{R}_j\cap\mathcal{F}_j=\mathcal{R}_{j+1}$. Hence $z\in\tau_1(\mathcal{R}_{j+1})$. A similar derivation gives $\tau_2(\mathcal{F}_{j+1})=\mathcal{G}_{j+1}$. \qed
head: environment

label: lemma:stabilize
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:stabilize}
		There is a non-negative integer $\alpha$ such that $\mathcal{R}_{j}=\mathcal{F}_{j}$ for every $j \ge \alpha$ and $\tau_1(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha})=\tau_2(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}) =\mathcal{G}_\alpha$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since the subspaces $\mathcal{R}_0$ and $\mathcal{F}_0$ are of finite dimension $m$, both chains stabilize, that is, there exist non-negative integers $\alpha_1$ and $\alpha_2$ such that for any $j_1\geq\alpha_1$ and $j_2\geq\alpha_2$ we have $\mathcal{R}_{j_1}=\mathcal{R}_{j_1+1}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{j_2}=\mathcal{F}_{j_2+1}$. Let $\alpha:=\max \{\alpha_1,\alpha_2\}$. We then have $\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}=\mathcal{R}_{\alpha+1}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{\alpha}=\mathcal{F}_{\alpha+1}$. Lemma \ref{lemma:chain-property} and the definition of $\alpha$ give $\mathcal{R}_{\alpha+1}\subset \mathcal{R}_\alpha\cap\mathcal{F}_\alpha\subset \mathcal{R}_{\alpha}=\mathcal{R}_{\alpha+1}$. This implies $\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}=\mathcal{R}_\alpha\cap\mathcal{F}_\alpha$. Similarly we get $\mathcal{F}_{\alpha}=\mathcal{R}_\alpha\cap\mathcal{F}_\alpha$. It follows that $\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}=\mathcal{F}_{\alpha}$. The equality $\tau_1(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha})=\tau_2(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha})= \mathcal{G}_\alpha$ is immediate from Lemma \ref{lemma:chain-property}. \qed
head: environment

label: lemma:W_alpha
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:W_alpha}
In addition to the hypotheses of Proposition \ref{prop:E<=n-d}, suppose $\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)>n-d$. Then there is a subspace $\mathcal{W}_\alpha$ of $\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}$ of dimension $[\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)-(n-d)]$ such that $\dim(\tau_1(\mathcal{W}_\alpha)+\tau_2(\mathcal{W}_\alpha))=2\dim(\mathcal{W}_\alpha)$.
head: environment
name: $\cW_\alpha$-Initialization

label: eq:UcapH
title: Proof
body_md:
By Lemma \ref{lemma:stabilize} and the rank-plus-nullity theorem we have
		\begin{align*}                           
		\dim(\ker(\tau_1|_{\mathcal{R}_\alpha}))=\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)-\dim(\mathcal{G}_{\alpha})=\dim(\ker(\tau_2|_{\mathcal{R}_\alpha}))
		\end{align*} Moreover, by hypothesis $\operatorname{rank}(\tau_1|_{\mathcal{R}_\alpha}) \ge \dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)-(n-2d)>d$. Hence $$(n-d)+\dim(\mathcal{G}_{\alpha})-\dim(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha})=\operatorname{rank}(\tau_1|_{\mathcal{R}_\alpha})-d>0$$ Since $\dim (\mathcal{U}_{\tau_1,\tau_2}^{\operatorname{cl}}) = \dim (\mathcal{U}_{\tau_1,\tau_2}) \le n-d$ and $\dim (\mathscr{E}_{(\tau_1,\tau_2),1}) \le n-d$ as well,  Lemma \ref{lemma:subspaces_intersect_subspace} gives a subspace $\mathcal{H}$ of $\mathcal{R}_\alpha$ of dimension $\dim(\mathcal{G}_{\alpha})$, such that $\mathcal{H} \cap \ker(\tau_1|_{\mathcal{R}_\alpha}) = \mathcal{H} \cap \ker(\tau_2|_{\mathcal{R}_\alpha})=0$ and 
					\begin{align}
	    	\dim(\mathcal{U}^{\operatorname{cl}}_{\tau_1,\tau_2}\cap\mathcal{H})\le (n-d)+\dim(\mathcal{G}_\alpha)-\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)\label{eq:UcapH} \\
			\dim(\mathscr{E}_{(\tau_1,\tau_2),1}\cap\mathcal{H})\le (n-d)+\dim(\mathcal{G}_\alpha)-\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)\label{eq:E1capH} 			
		\end{align} Since $\tau_1(\mathcal{H})=\mathcal{G}_\alpha=\tau_2(\mathcal{H})$ we have that $\tau_\mathcal{H}:=(\tau_1|_\mathcal{H})^{-1}\tau_2|_\mathcal{H}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal{H}$. We are going to get our subspace $\mathcal{W}_\alpha$ by applying Lemma \ref{lemma:lemma5ofHS} with ambient space $\mathcal{H}$, $\mathbb{C}$-linear map $\tau_\mathcal{H}$ and subspace dimension $[\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)-(n-d)]$, this number being positive by hypothesis. There are two things we need to check, the first being that $\dim (\mathcal{H}) \ge 2 [\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)-(n-d)]$. Indeed, this is true because  
	 \begin{align*}
			\dim(\mathcal{H})\geq 2[\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)-(n-d)]
			&\Leftrightarrow 2n-2d\geq \dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)+\dim(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha})-\dim(\mathcal{G}_\alpha)\\
			&\Leftrightarrow 2n-2d\geq \dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)+\dim(\ker(\tau_1|_{\mathcal{R}_\alpha})) \\
			&\Leftarrow 2n-2d\geq \dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)+\dim(\ker(\tau_1)) \\
			&\Leftrightarrow (\operatorname{rank}(\tau_1)-2d) + (n-\dim(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha}))\geq 0
		\end{align*} and the last inequality is true by hypothesis. The second thing that we need to check is that for any $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$ 
		\begin{align*}                  
			\dim(\mathscr{E}_{\tau_\mathcal{H},\lambda})\leq\dim(\mathcal{H})-[\dim(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha})-(n-d)]
		\end{align*}
When $\lambda=0$, we have $\mathscr{E}_{\tau_\mathcal{H},0} = \ker(\tau_\mathcal{H})=0$, because $\tau_\mathcal{H}$ is an isomorphism. When $\lambda\neq 0$, 
$v \in \mathscr{E}_{\tau_\mathcal{H},\lambda}$ is equivalent to $\tau_1|_\mathcal{H}(v)=\lambda\tau_2|_\mathcal{H}(v)$ or equivalently $v\in(\mathcal{U}_{\tau_1,\tau_2}\cap\mathcal{H}) \cup (\mathscr{E}_{(\tau_1,\tau_2),1} \cap \mathcal{H})$. This shows that $\mathscr{E}_{\tau_\mathcal{H},\lambda}$ lives in $(\mathcal{U}_{\tau_1,\tau_2}^{\operatorname{cl}}\cap\mathcal{H}) \cup (\mathscr{E}_{(\tau_1,\tau_2),1} \cap \mathcal{H})$ and as per \eqref{eq:UcapH} and \eqref{eq:E1capH} that latter set has dimension at most $\dim (\mathcal{H}) -[\dim(\mathcal{R}_\alpha)-(n-d)]$. 

Now Lemma \ref{lemma:lemma5ofHS} gives a subspace $\mathcal{W}_\alpha$ of $\mathcal{H}$ of dimension $[\dim(\mathcal{R}_{\alpha})-(n-d)]$ such that $\dim(\mathcal{W}_\alpha+\tau_\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{W}_\alpha))=2\dim(\mathcal{W}_\alpha)$. Since $\tau_1|_\mathcal{H}$ is an isomorphism from $\mathcal{H}$ to $\mathcal{G}_{\alpha}$ and $\mathcal{W}_\alpha+\tau_\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{W}_\alpha)$ is a subspace of $\mathcal{H}$, we have that $\mathcal{W}_\alpha+\tau_\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{W}_\alpha) \cong \tau_1|_\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{W}_\alpha+\tau_\mathcal{H}(\mathcal{W}_\alpha)) = \tau_1(\mathcal{W}_\alpha) + \tau_2(\mathcal{W}_\alpha)$. That is, $\dim (\tau_1(\mathcal{W}_\alpha) + \tau_2(\mathcal{W}_\alpha)) = 2 \dim (\mathcal{W}_\alpha)$. \qed
head: environment
